evidence.evidence: This domain interface is broken upon activation, allowing nucleophile access.
evidence.limits: Primary bovine C3 structure. Do not use the separately retracted human C3b paper. Covalent surface deposition is supported, universal exact atom-by-atom activation path not asserted.

evidence.evidence: provides energy for substrate carboxylation when it is oxidized to vitamin K2,3-epoxide
evidence.limits: 2026 primary cryo-EM structures and 2000 primary biochemical study support coupled oxygenation/carboxylation. Old cysteine-base assignment is not adopted; exact base species and free carbanion lifetime remain qualified.

evidence.evidence: the peptide backbone of residues 65-67 has condensed to form a five-membered heterocyclic ring
evidence.limits: Trapped GFP Y66L intermediate by crystallography and mass spectrometry. Mutation-specific step ordering is not universalized.

evidence.evidence: a nucleophilic attack on CO2 by the reactive zinc-bound hydroxide
evidence.limits: Primary substrate-bound holo/apo structures support CO2 orientation. Card does not split carbonic anhydrase metal/class variants.

evidence.evidence: the formation of an Fe(IV) oxo radical cation
evidence.limits: Primary electrochemistry study explicitly gives two-peroxide heme cycle in results/discussion. No claim of direct electron tunneling or individual-molecule catalysis from disputed spikes.

evidence.evidence: the nitrile is activated by coordination to the LS FeIII
evidence.limits: EPR/MCD/absorption-calibrated DFT primary study. Proposed cyclic sulfenate route is computationally favored, not universally directly observed; independent nitrilase nitrogen-releasing path is excluded.

evidence.evidence: visualize different stages of persulfide transfer from Cys381NFS1 to Cys138ISCU2
evidence.limits: Primary anaerobic cryo-EM plus biochemistry. Double sulfur density may be averaging rather than one chemical intermediate and is not asserted as a unique intermediate.

evidence.evidence: These results support a two-base racemization mechanism involving Y265 and K39.
evidence.limits: Primary mutants, isotope effects, quinonoid absorbance and substrate-analogue structures. Boundary requires PLP covalent aldimine chemistry; mere different amino acid is not counted.

evidence.evidence: uses fluoride to substitute the hydroxide acting as the co-substrate
evidence.limits: Primary 1.42 Å inhibited substrate-bound urease structure. Not an unmodified time-resolved turnover observation; substrate coordination and nucleophile role interpreted with this limit.

evidence.evidence: closes openings and entraps the prey proteinase
evidence.limits: Eight primary cryo-EM structures. Large substrate access is blocked while small substrates can remain accessible, distinguishing serpin active-site deformation.

evidence.evidence: the 3′ OH of GTP directly attacks the α-phosphate group
evidence.limits: PMC direct open returned CAPTCHA; retrieved primary search excerpt states triphosphorylated RNA can bypass ATP activation. Successive terminal-triphosphate extension must be distinguished from single ligation.

evidence.evidence: RNA is tethered to TGT through the side chain of Asp280
evidence.limits: Official primary structure deposition and reproduced author abstract were opened; chemical competence is stated, not merely inferred from a trapped adduct.

evidence.evidence: donating the methyl group to homocysteine to generate methionine and cob(I)alamin
evidence.limits: Structural primary author abstract retrieved in search; source addresses catalytic carrier and reductive reactivation domain.

evidence.evidence: All three terminators encode the canonical G:C-rich stem-loop hairpin element
evidence.limits: Primary single-molecule results; sequence-dependent load behavior does not establish one universal shearing or hypertranslocation pathway.

evidence.evidence: Reactivation requires RNA transcript cleavage.
evidence.limits: Primary cryo-EM structures span backtracking, GreB binding, cleavage and reactivation. RNA internal cleavage is not free-end exonucleolysis.

evidence.evidence: the location of the ribosome synthesizing the leader peptide is communicated to the RNA polymerase
evidence.limits: Primary mutation and in vitro transcription studies; RNA alternatives also supported by primary structural probing PMID118451. Do not generalize to uncoupled eukaryotic transcription.

evidence.evidence: autokinase, phosphotransfer, and phosphatase activities
evidence.limits: Primary HK853/RR468 complex and phosphorylation studies; domain names do not imply identical outputs across systems.

evidence.evidence: the protein template can switch its base specificity between ATP and CTP
evidence.limits: 2002 structures alone left RNA-terminal selection unresolved. Opened 2004 primary abstract and mutations support protein recognition of terminal CC and incoming ATP; kinetics of every transition not claimed.

evidence.evidence: the hydroxy O atom comes from O2, but not from H2O
evidence.limits: Isotope-labeling primary study establishes oxygen source and carbinolamide route; separate primary lyase structures and mutants support N-dealkylation.

evidence.evidence: followed by the synthesis of atypical 1,6-anhydro-GlcNAc derivatives
evidence.limits: Primary LtgA in-crystal and mass-spectrometric study includes initial hydrolytic intermediate/alternative mechanism. Card deliberately does not assert universal exclusion of water or one oxazolinium path.
